name: HNRNPA1-related Adult-Onset Distal Myopathy
aliases: Adult-Onset Distal Myopathy due to HNRNPA1 Mutation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for HNRNPA1-related Distal Myopathy

criteria.description: Adult-onset distal muscle weakness predominantly affecting distal lower limbs
Identification of pathogenic HNRNPA1 gene mutation
Muscle biopsy showing rimmed vacuoles and myopathic changes
EMG demonstrating myopathic motor unit potentials
Positive family history of adult-onset distal myopathy or related neuromuscular disorder

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of adult-onset distal muscle weakness with pathogenic HNRNPA1 mutation and supportive muscle biopsy findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, genetic, and pathological data; EMG and family history support but are not mandatory.

common.symptomName: Weakness of the intrinsic hand muscles

laboratory: Elevated serum creatine kinase (mild to moderate elevation)
imaging: Muscle MRI showing selective distal muscle atrophy and fatty replacement
other: Muscle biopsy demonstrating rimmed vacuoles, fiber size variation, and myopathic changes
Electromyography showing myopathic motor unit potentials

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of multisystem proteinopathy with inclusion body myopathy, Paget disease, and frontotemporal dementia
Variable age of onset with both proximal and distal weakness
Muscle biopsy may show different histopathological features

redFlags: Severe dysphagia with risk of aspiration
references: Kim HJ, et al. HNRNPA1 mutations cause adult-onset distal myopathy. Neurology. 2013;81(15):1322-1330.
Orphanet: HNRNPA1-related adult-onset distal myopathy. ORPHA:399086.
Mackenzie IR, et al. Pathology and genetics of distal myopathies. Neuropathol Appl Neurobiol. 2017;43(1):3-20.
